subject.title: feat: cross-gateway sessions_send and sessions_spawn via gateway.peers

question: Should OpenClaw expose direct cross-gateway session routing from agent tools via `gateway.peers` / `gatewayUrl`, and what peer trust model should gate it?
rationale: The PR changes an operator-grade gateway security boundary and persistent config surface, so automation cannot choose whether this belongs as a narrow tool feature, a broader federation design, or an external/plugin pattern.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow peer contract
options.body: Approve a specific peer-auth model and require this PR to be repaired around the existing URL/auth hardening before any merge.

options.title: Defer to federation design
options.body: Pause or close this PR and track the work under the broader cross-gateway federation design issue instead.

options.title: Keep current isolation model
options.body: Decline direct agent-tool gateway routing for now and document supported operator-managed remote gateway alternatives.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrow peer contract
recommendation.body: Approve a specific peer-auth model and require this PR to be repaired around the existing URL/auth hardening before any merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The most relevant prior history is the gateway URL override and gateway authorization hardening that this PR would need to preserve or intentionally redesign.
